recipe: Organize most of your code within a features folder, where each feature folder contains only code specific to that feature, keeping it separated from shared components.
trigger_condition: When structuring a React/TypeScript application to improve scalability and maintainability.
evidence: For easy scalability and maintenance, organize most of the code within the features folder.

recipe: Only include the subfolders (api, assets, components, hooks, stores, types, utils) within a feature that are actually necessary for that feature.
trigger_condition: When creating a new feature folder and deciding which subdirectories to add.
evidence: You don't need all of these folders for every feature. Only include the ones that are necessary for the feature.

recipe: If multiple features share API calls, extract them into a dedicated top-level api folder instead of duplicating them inside each feature.
trigger_condition: When you have a lot of shared API calls between features.
evidence: In some cases it might be more practical to keep all API calls outside of the features folders in a dedicated `api` folder where all API calls are defined.

recipe: Import files directly from their source modules rather than using barrel files, to preserve Vite tree-shaking and avoid performance issues.
trigger_condition: When exporting or importing modules from feature folders in a Vite-based project.
evidence: it can cause issues for Vite to do tree shaking and can lead to performance issues. Therefore, it is recommended to import the files directly.

recipe: Avoid importing directly from one feature into another; instead, compose different features at the application level to keep each feature independent.
trigger_condition: When two or more features need to work together in the same application.
evidence: It might not be a good idea to import across the features. Instead, compose different features at the application level.

recipe: Configure ESLint's import/no-restricted-paths rule with zones that target each feature folder and exclude only itself, to forbid cross-feature imports.

recipe: Enforce a unidirectional import architecture where code flows from shared parts to features to app (shared -> features -> app), and use ESLint import/no-restricted-paths to enforce it.
trigger_condition: When you want to make your codebase more predictable and easier to understand by controlling import direction across layers.
evidence: You might also want to enforce unidirectional codebase architecture. This means that the code should flow in one direction, from shared parts of the code to the application (shared -> features -> app).
